title: Games to Explore After Fate Trigger
description: Compare selected games for Fate Trigger readers, with clear reasons to explore each setting and links to independent guides.
intro: Fate Trigger combines individual ability choices with team decisions. These guides help compare hero-led matches, tactical teamwork, and extraction objectives without treating their rules as interchangeable.
disclosure: These independent guide websites are maintained by the same operator. Recommendations are editorial suggestions, not official partnerships or endorsements. Official game sources are listed separately.

entries.name: Marvel Rivals
entries.reason: Read about hero roles and team combinations in a competitive shooter. This is a useful destination for players interested in how one character choice changes a team.
entries.difference: Marvel Rivals centres on team-based hero combat and role combinations; Fate Trigger centres on ability-driven shooting in a battle-royale setting. Similar interests do not imply identical mechanics or multiplayer support.

entries.name: WARDOGS
entries.reason: Explore tactical squad roles and coordinated shooting. Its guide helps you compare team organisation rather than assuming hero abilities or extraction rules carry across games.
entries.difference: WARDOGS centres on tactical shooting and coordinated squad play; Fate Trigger centres on ability-driven shooting in a battle-royale setting. Similar interests do not imply identical mechanics or multiplayer support.

entries.name: Beautiful Light
entries.reason: Research a shooter where extraction objectives meet horror imagery. Consider it for armed team encounters and tension rather than for a peaceful exploration loop.
entries.difference: Beautiful Light centres on tactical extraction shooting with horror elements; Fate Trigger centres on ability-driven shooting in a battle-royale setting. Similar interests do not imply identical mechanics or multiplayer support.
